beats.headline: First cat down the stairs
beats.text: Carl carries me down, and the dungeon gives him a Legendary Pet Box for it, which is fair, and gives me a Legendary Quadruped Box of my own, which is more than fair. His box has a biscuit in it. An Enhanced Pet Biscuit. I take it out of his hand, because it is obviously for me, and I melt into a heap of goo, and I get up talking. I have a great deal to say.

beats.headline: GC BWR NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
beats.text: I learn Magic Missile. I also have the highest stat total in the party, which makes me party leader, which anyone could have predicted. My first act is to give the party a proper name: the Royal Court of Princess Donut. There is an inauguration. Carl does not take it seriously enough, but there is an inauguration.

beats.headline: She equips a crown with an ominous description
beats.text: Mordecai says read the description first. Mordecai says a great many things. It is a crown, it is dark and smoky and exactly my colour, and it came out of my box, which has the word Legendary on it. It has a vulgar name, which is not my fault. It says something about the Blood Sultanate and a line of succession, eight floors down. I am already a princess. I do not see how being in line for anything could be a demotion. Carl is making his face.

beats.headline: I need you, Carl
beats.text: Carl tries to leave the party, so I have to say it. It is like waking from a long dream and remembering you were something else. I am a grand champion and I must act like one. But sitting in his lap watching him get fragged in Call of Duty? I liked that too. He is truly terrible at that game. I am scared. I do not want to be alone, and neither does he. I saw him on Craigslist looking at apartments that allow cats. He was planning to catnap me. It would not have worked. Miss Beatrice's father would have had me back right away.

beats.headline: The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly
beats.text: I am one of the first hundred crawlers to reach level three in Magic Missile, so I get a gold box, and in it is a little silver butterfly charm for my collar. It jingles. Carl says birds will hear me coming. It is adorable and I am wearing it. Plus four to Light on Your Feet, so I can reach the very top of the play tubes. The caretaker here calls me Your Highness and orders me fresh salmon. I want on that show. Carl says we are not getting on it.

beats.headline: That will be a no
beats.text: The door has put itself back together and locked us in behind glowing bars. Then a very large lady comes out of the garbage, and Carl says she is a person, like she was in her house when it happened, and we should help her. That will be a no. I shoot her. She vomits cockroaches at us. I jump to the top of a garbage heap and keep firing, and then it will not let me drink another potion, so Carl is shouting at me to use my claws. She is almost dead. I tell him he can kill them when he kills her.

beats.headline: Miss Beatrice is my agent
beats.text: My Bronze Boss Box has a spell book in it and I learn it at once, and it is Torch. A curl of light. Mordecai says I must read things first; I say it is a stupid spell. But then he tells us about the other show, where the commentators interview crawlers after boss fights. We must be on it. Carl says he is not my agent. Of course not. Miss Beatrice is my agent, and she is halfway around the world, so we will find her when the dungeon is small enough, around the fifth or sixth floor. Carl and Mordecai exchange a look.

beats.headline: What if it hits me back
beats.text: Carl says my missiles run out too quickly and I must train with my claws. I have never done anything like that. I am scared of getting hurt. I am only a few generations shy of a tiger. He says my grandfather was also my uncle. Then we find the dead lady, and I say some imbecile with a gun does not scare me and we should hunt this vile killer down, and Carl agrees. So now I am scared of him. What if he is one of those murder hobos?

beats.headline: Thirty-seven charisma
beats.text: Carl wants to do the talking because he has the tattoo. I have a 37 in charisma. I name three goblins B.A., Face and Murdock, and B.A. takes us to the engineers. The shamanka with fifty things in her face calls Carl a monkey, so I ask her whether it is a daddy thing, and she sits down and cries, and I sit in her lap. I name her Rory and the other one Lorelai. They build Carl a chopper for two bags of llama meth and the promise of where to find more. I ask Rory if she would like to come with us. She cannot.

beats.headline: Just like I planned
beats.text: The sidecar seat is a skull, so I have the engineers add another layer of fur and paint the backrest purple. When the goblin lady asks Carl if he wants some fun before we go, I tell her we are on a schedule and banging monster girls is not the narrative we are going for. Rory asks where we got the drugs and I tell her, and every goblin in the room goes off to war with the llamas. Just like I planned. Now there is only the door at the end of the room, and I could really use another boss box.

beats.headline: What vile monster puts babies there
beats.text: There were babies in the boss room, quite cute ones, and I think Carl hit one with the cart. He keeps saying goddamnit. It is not as if they did not have it coming. He did not ask to be here. They are goblins! What kind of vile monster sticks babies in the boss room anyway? We are both level eight, which he may thank me for, and my charisma is 39. We did not get our faces up big this time, which is a shame. I must admit, I do like it when he blows stuff up. I like it a lot.

beats.headline: A disqualifying mark
beats.text: They have branded me. A gold splotch on my back, over my right shoulder blade, glowing through my fur. It is a disqualifying mark, Carl! I am damaged! My Boss Box, at least, has my first armor: an Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, silver scale with a slot for my tail, plus two Dexterity. Carl says it looks great and does not cover the tattoo, not even close. My Beguiler Box has a tome called Minion Army, which costs fifty spell points. I have twenty-four. It will not even let me read it.

beats.headline: An American hero, briefly
beats.text: The man who killed Rebecca W is in the women's bathroom, and I say so. Then he tells his story, about his partner being shot, and I am devastated for him, and I tell Carl in the chat that Frank is an American hero. Carl tells me not to fire. They try to shoot us both and freeze where they stand. When we are running, I tell Carl that if we do not stop them they will hurt somebody else. He stops dead in the hallway and looks at me as though I have said something unusual.

beats.headline: Claws are not ladylike
beats.text: Carl hits and I shoot, and we are becoming very good at it; I ride his shoulder and hide in his cloak when something spits poison. Then I bat a lizard's head across the hall and it cracks the wall, and Carl says my strength is eighteen to his nine and I should practise with my claws. I could swipe through steel, apparently. Fighting with one's claws is inelegant. It is not ladylike. With Magic Missile I do not get blood on me like a common house cat. I do not answer him.

beats.headline: I used my claws, like he said
beats.text: The Juicer has Carl by the wrist and the throat and his health is going, and my missile barely tickles. So I jump, claws out, onto that ridiculous shoulder and bite through one of the veins in his neck. The blood comes out like a fountain. He slaps me into the far wall and my leg breaks. I am badly hurt, and I say so at some length, and I ask Carl to tell Miss Beatrice I fought bravely. Then I take one of my own potions. He tells me to get up and help him loot.

beats.headline: Born a cat
beats.text: Mordecai talks about picking races and classes as though I would consider changing. I am already one of God's most perfect creatures. I was born a cat and I will die a cat, and I shall insist that Carl choose a cat race too. Carl says he is staying human. Then I read my new spell book. Puddle Jumper: myself and up to three others, anywhere I can see, for twenty mana and a five-hour cooldown. Carl asks if I read the description first. Mordecai answers for me.

beats.headline: He always stays
beats.text: The forcefield is down and Carl asks me whether we stick with these people or do our own thing. As if I do not know what he is going to do before he does. So I tell him the sensible version: we set them up somewhere safe, keep our own party, make a group chat, and fetch them when we find the next stairs. If it were up to me I would leave them all. But he is a softy, and if he turns into a cat on the third floor we shall need someone with thumbs.

beats.headline: We are going to kill them with style
beats.text: Every cat show I have ever done is an interview. I was bred for this. So I ask Lexis about the tone, I tell Carl to let me talk and not to be surly, and I walk onto the set and roll over for them. I explain the monarchy, and I wink. When Odette asks what is next, I stand up on my pillow and tell them all to follow us, because whatever we face, we will not just kill it. We will kill it with style. After thirty seconds they are still screaming.

beats.headline: Dungeon Book of the Floor Club
beats.text: Thanks to my boss box I am a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, which mails me one spell book per level, and the mailbox opens for me and not for Carl. I read it at once. Second Chance: raise a dead monster lower than me to fight for us for a minute a level. It is disgusting; the dead are bad enough without moaning. Then Carl says I could raise a dingo, have it kill another dingo, and raise that one too. A zombie dog army. This is the best spell ever.

beats.headline: My first follower
beats.text: We are on the show, finally, for less than fifteen seconds: me shouting that it is coming, me firing point-blank into pigs, Imani dropping something unmentionable. Two shows in one day! Carl says I am obsessing and it will get us killed, which is unfair. Then the announcement ends and the numbers turn on. A follower. My first follower. A view! Carl points out that the viewer is watching me right now, and I sit down, lick my paw and remark that it was quite the battle today.

beats.headline: Second Chance, for practice
beats.text: I have fourteen mana and Carl asks, so I raise a dead clurichaun. It sways and moans. I tell it to rip up its friends, and it does, groaning the whole time. Most unpleasant. After that, every time we clear a room I raise one and Carl practises hitting it with a slingshot, which does hardly any damage. My Second Chance reaches level three, so they last three minutes. I find a pamphlet about becoming a Rev-Up consultant, which says it is not a pyramid. Carl says it is easier to kill them and take it all, and it is: no upline, no seed investment.

beats.headline: Plan Pied Piper
beats.text: I Puddle Jumper into their filling room, right between the two fairy managers, and they are charmed at once, though the forty workers stay red. So, plan Pied Piper. I tell the fairies a terrible story about dingoes and walk them all into the next room to see, the workers too, and leave the workers there. Carl throws his jugs. I catch one of the fairies out of the air like a bird. The other one takes longer, because Carl insists on his slingshot. My first solo mission. I would be fine crawling this dungeon by myself.

beats.headline: I lied before
beats.text: The smoothie has made me drunk. I tell Carl that if we die, I want him to know I love him. Not as much as Miss Beatrice, who is my person, but I love him. Then he sends a zombie with a bomb into the boss's room and pulls a table over us and tells me I will be okay, that I should go back to Brandon. No. I lied before. I will not be fine on my own. I need him.

beats.headline: She drags him out by the cloak
beats.text: The boss is dead, the room is on fire, and Carl is lying in the rubble telling me he cannot hear me. So I write it in capitals. He cannot stand either, apparently, so I take him by the cloak and drag him out, and he is much heavier than he looks. He croaks something about a scroll, and I use one of the healing scrolls. He says I saved him again. That is what I do. I do not say the next part out loud: our views went way up.

beats.headline: Dungeon Gold Rush
beats.text: We get a Platinum Lucky Bastard Box for hurting something more than seventy-five levels above us, and inside is a scratch-off ticket. Mine is Dungeon Gold Rush: scratch one spot an hour, and my next attack might drop five thousand coins. It will not work in a safe room, and Carl makes me hand it over so he can read the back, and then says we will talk about it. Why must he always be so pessimistic? His ticket casts either a fireball or custard, so I have Qwist bring me custard. Not strawberry. Vanilla.

beats.headline: Tailgunner on the Bomb Chicken
beats.text: I sit backward on a tall seat behind the launcher, like a tailgunner, and I have just hit one trillion views when Imani opens the door. Bombs away. The chain from the black lever. Burn, baby, burn. The oil from the red lever. Then Carl tells me to jump off a moving vehicle. Are you crazy? I jump. I cast Puddle Jumper when he says, and the monster goes into the hole, and we get no experience at all. Carl, you broke the game.

beats.headline: I do the talking
beats.text: This boat heaves more than the last one, and I am going to puke on television. Carl brings up his pillow. That was different; I did that on purpose. The crowd is all boys chanting glurp, and I remind Carl of our arrangement: he sits there and looks angry, and I do the talking. Then he climbs over the table and walks out, and I tell him he is going to get us in trouble. Twice. When we sit back down, he says he is the one who talks this time.

beats.headline: I heard him
beats.text: Back in the safe room I cannot stop talking. Yvette is a pretty name, and it's sad, but I'm also kind of relieved: her mother killed her, so Carl didn't. And the orc said we broke the record. Then I tell Carl the other thing. Not what the orc said about the ninth floor. What Mordecai said, when he told Carl he should leave me when we get to that floor. I heard him. Carl says to worry about getting to the third floor first. Okay.

beats.headline: She adopts a dinosaur
beats.text: There is a reward room on the second floor with a cage in it, and in the cage is a pet-class mob, and the pet-class mob is my son. I did not know that until I saw him. He is called Mongo. He is mine, and that is the end of the discussion.

beats.headline: Mongo becomes a Royal Steed
beats.text: Who knew being a mother would be this difficult? Mongo bites my nose over and over. I show him how a grub opens, and we teach him attack and come, and attack becomes sic 'em. Then, outside the stair room, a hornet grabs my son and lifts him toward its mouth, and I take its head off. Then I have a new menu: Mongo the Mongoliensis, pet of Grand Champion Best in Dungeon Princess Donut, title Royal Steed. We tamed Mongo. Then he bites me on the nose.

beats.headline: Cat, and a Former Child Actor
beats.text: Odette suggested it, so obviously it is a good idea: a class that lets me choose another class at every level. I also arrange for Mordecai to be my manager. He is thrilled. He does not show it, but he is. My constitution is apparently far too low for what Carl calls melee, so I will be fighting with charisma, spells and the audience, which is how it should be done.

beats.headline: Asleep through the paperwork
beats.text: I curl up with Mongo and fall asleep while Carl reads every race there is. Staying a cat gives me Night Vision, Slash Attack, Cat-like Reflexes and something called 9 Lives, which halves the first nine physical hits I take each day. When I wake up I ask Carl if he grew elf ears. He did not. He is still human, which is boring. He says he is a Primal. That sounds like a caveman, and he smells exactly the same.

beats.headline: Not my child, he says
beats.text: My Earth box is lovely: a Sea Breeze candle and a cat tree fancier than the one at home, which Carl will assemble. My hobby potion makes me a scutelliphile, which sounds obscene. Outside, I show my son how a lady takes a lemur off a roof, and my collar jingles, and Mongo screeches, and I get it anyway. Carl says Mongo is not my child, he is a pet, and we do not risk our lives for pets. That was very hurtful. Then I tell him where the circus tents are. He calls me partner. Okay. Partner.

beats.headline: She sees the elf lady first
beats.text: I make the hole bigger so my Puddle Jumper can see the sky, and there she is on the street, waiting like she knows we are here: the elf lady from the poster, naked except for a quite lovely thong, covered in tattoos that swim around like a fishbowl. Her dot is white. I get too scared to examine her. I do not like tattoos. When she reaches out to pet me, I growl. We want nothing to do with her and her circus freak friends, and I tell her so.

beats.headline: Zombie lions
beats.text: Carl shouts spells at me and I cast them. Second Chance, ten points, on the lion he pulled apart, and it gets up and rips the throat out of its friend. Then that one gets up too, and I give it two clockwork copies for twenty-six points and a mana potion. The last lion swipes at my son, and I shoot it dead with a magic missile. He does not even notice. We are both level fourteen. I do not like that lady, even if her dot is white.

beats.headline: Asleep for all of it
beats.text: I wake at dawn in a chair in a strange building, level 15, having done nothing whatsoever, and Mongo is enormous. I dreamed Ferdinand came to visit and turned into a porcupine, which was unpleasant. Carl did not kill the boss. If I had been awake we would have done things differently. He says the producers now want us alive. Until the sixth floor, when they write something to get us killed. We are guest stars, Carl, and a show cannot keep guest stars more interesting than its main character. That is why they killed Barb. GUESSING THE PLOTLINES OF TELEVISION SHOWS IS MY SUPER POWER.

beats.headline: A master shopper
beats.text: Shopkeepers get sweetness and sugar, and they love me for it. It takes five general stores to sell everything, and we come away with about fifty thousand gold. The Artist Alley Merchant class I chose to emulate did not give me its buying discount, but I have the extra fifteen percent when I sell, and I planned it that way. Miss Beatrice did not call me Princess Money Bags for nothing. Carl says it was Money Pit. We spend fifteen thousand on a pet carrier for my son, who needs his rest. I relent.

beats.headline: The Boomy Boy
beats.text: Carl and I have a playbook now. Either of us may call a play and the other follows without argument. Panic is the first: Carl casts Fear, I hit the mob with a missile. Today we add another. My Acute Ears tell us something is waiting around the corner, a manta ray thing called the Dispenser that drops off a wall, and I send two reanimated brain boilers at it, then a clockwork Mongo with a stick of dynamite in each hand. The whole fight takes under a minute. The real Mongo screams. We call it the Boomy Boy.

beats.headline: A Dirty Shirley, in a bowl
beats.text: Mama needs a night off, so I order Miss Beatrice's kryptonite, the Dirty Shirley, in a bowl. Vodka is gross. I only ate the cherries. And a little more. The pharmacist looks to me like a floating, talking anteater, and I talk him down to three bottles and a potion to stop the room being wavy, and I would like to know why Carl did not warn me. Then a notice arrives: my followers' box can be opened. I leave the men at the table for the dance floor, jump onto an ogre's shoulder, and we twirl.

beats.headline: Pustule has excellent hearing
beats.text: The hobgoblin at the explosives booth is ugly. Like really ugly. I whisper it to Carl, and she says she has excellent hearing. So I start over. Oh sweetie, we got off on the wrong foot; we will be buying a great deal from you, and I would really like us to be friends. Her last friend was a muskrat called Tiff. Her mother bit the head off a vorpal muskrat, which killed her. By the end I have fifteen hundred gold down to a thousand. On the way out she calls after us again: excellent hearing.

beats.headline: GumGum died because of us
beats.text: She was a nice lady, for an orc, and she was doing the right thing. They probably killed her because we took her quest. So we are finishing it, and I tell Mordecai there is nothing he can do to stop us. I ask Fitz how he knew about the krasue, and he tells us GumGum's mother was one of those ladies, and bled to death alone on her own stoop. Miss Beatrice's picture goes by my cat tree. I make Carl promise not to let me die alone. Then something hits the roof right above our heads.

beats.headline: The only one still awake
beats.text: Carl jumps into a swimming pool full of dead boss and the boss goes off like a potato in a microwave. I watch him sail over the street spinning like a pinwheel. So I fetch the neighbourhood map, missile two of the last three, set Mongo on the third, jump to the roof and heal Carl with a scroll. I am covered in three inches of guts. Mongo is level 12. We have a new rule: no throwing explosives while blind. And I need a shower before our interview.

beats.headline: Will she leave Carl for Bea
beats.text: A caller in a top hat, Chappy, asks me what happens if Miss Beatrice is alive and shows up. Am I really going to leave Carl for her? The studio has already bucked once tonight, and I was sick all down my front. Now this. When we reunite with Miss Beatrice we will all work together. It will be like before. He seems perplexed and asks Carl, who mumbles something about bridges. Then the host breaks in with news.

beats.headline: Named the Oak Fell
beats.text: The city elves outside a corrupt temple call me a disgusting, vile blasphemer, and I have done nothing. It is the anklet: the Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak, which Carl gave me and which I always said was ugly. I show them my backside, which is award-winning. On Carl's word I shake my back leg, the beads rattle, and they come apart; one of them claws her own face bloody. Then they eat acorns and glow, and their leader announces who I am. Donut, the Oak Fell. The Death Upon Us All. She Who Ends.

beats.headline: Since when can the news lie
beats.text: The recap puts me against Cici and Gustavo 3 with a lightning bolt between us, as though I had thrown down a gauntlet at Lucia Mar's dogs. I have done no such thing. They play me at the bar, being rude about rottweilers, which was a remark and not a challenge. Then the girl herself, with bugs crawling in her eye sockets, says she will find me in the dungeon and her dogs will tear me apart. Carl, since when is the news allowed to lie? We would kill them easily, of course. I simply do not want those ugly skulls after my name.

beats.headline: She asked me to
beats.text: The burnt woman is Burgundy, from the stairs, one of the magistrate's assistants, and one of those things: a person by day, a krasue at night. Carl wants to heal her. She says healing will only turn her back, and to kill her while she is still mortal. So I stroke her hair and tell her it is going to be okay, sweetie, and ask about Featherfall. She tells us Miss Quill ran the city all along, and about a husband named Remex across the street. Then the room slumps and she slides away, begging. I hit her with a Magic Missile before she is gone.

beats.headline: He promised I would not die alone
beats.text: Carl's plan is to ring the warehouse with dynamite and go up alone to meet the lich while I wait outside. Absolutely not. He promised me I would not die alone, and he cannot keep that promise if he dies before me. We do this together. So the plan changes, and Katia gets the button. I tell him at the bottom of the ladder that I do not like this plan. Mongo stays in his carrier; he has proven he cannot be trusted to stay still. I ride up on Carl's shoulder.

beats.headline: I know she's dead
beats.text: Carl says we can save ourselves, or try for Katia and eighty other people with an idea that probably won't work. I don't know. Then I do: we try, because it is the right thing. We sit and watch a glass case float round a cracking gem while Remex tells his son he is coming. Carl says Remex was a crawler once. I do not want to become an NPC. Carl says he is proud of me for worrying about Katia; I tell him I just don't want Hekla mad at us. Then I tell him I am not as dumb as I pretend. I know she's dead.

beats.headline: It was my first item
beats.text: Carl wants the tiara off. I will lose five Intelligence, and my Sepsis debuff, and I really like it. And if I lose it somebody else gets it and we will have to fight them, and I do not want to hurt a person. But a man's arrows have just gone off in his quiver, and Carl says it might set my head on fire, and Katia says he is right. Oh, all right. It crumbles into dust before I can take it off. At the door I point out that Carl should have put his pants back on before we go straight to Odette's show.

beats.headline: An iron paw
beats.text: Odette shows a crawler dragging himself into a saferoom, the same one who was so rude to us in the quest chat. I am glad he survived; I felt kind of bad, because I blocked him. You cannot let people in your chatrooms get out of control. Then Quan Ch opens a Celestial box that he got for our hard work, and we get nothing, not even a Platinum. This is an outrage. Then the leaderboard: Carl sixth, me seventh, dear Hekla second, and that ugly Lucia Mar first. We are in the top ten!

beats.headline: Hooligan, on six minutes’ notice
beats.text: The moment we land on this filthy train, my Character Actor skill says I must pick a new class in six minutes or be given a random one, and the list is nothing like before. I DON'T LIKE THESE CHOICES, and I tell Mordecai so. He says Football Hooligan: a momentum bonus, team buffs, and a skill called Mascot that is all about Mongo. I get Mascot. I do not get Group Chant or Moving Riot. I get ten points of Constitution, and Guinness, which doubles my strength when I am drunk. So if there is fighting, we stop at the club first for a dirty Shirley.

beats.headline: Wendita, down to 37,500
beats.text: The Bopca says fifty thousand for a personal space and that it is not something they negotiate. Oh, sweetie. Everything is negotiable. She offers forty-five, I turn my back on her, and she says forty-four thousand, and then thirty-eight, and then 37,500, which is as low as the system will let her go, so I ask how much she has saved up. Carl says not to make her pay from her own pocket. I can feel her wavering. It is delicious. But we pay with the coupons from our boxes instead, and fifteen thousand gold on top, and she weeps and says she knew asking her to pay was only a test. A real princess would never do such a thing.

beats.headline: A spell called Hole
beats.text: A new tiara poofs onto my head: the Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita, white jewels instead of purple, three intelligence and better at spotting mobs on my map. It is not as good as the one I lost. Then the mailbox in the corner has my spellbook, and it is not Fireball. When am I going to get a good spell? I ask Mordecai whether I should read it or sell it, and he says read it. It is called Hole. At level one it is not thick enough to get through most doors.

beats.headline: Suitcase number eight
beats.text: The Yellow Line Reward Room is a porter's hatch and shelves of suitcases, one prize per crawler per line. I am suitcase number eight. It is just like Deal or No Deal. Carl's is somebody's lingerie and three potions, one of them invisibility. Mine is full of ants that are on fire. Thousands. The bar goes up, the moonshine explodes, my tail is burning, and poor Vernon is just gone under them. I cast Heal Pet on Mongo and we jump out onto the platform as the doors shut. That was the worst prize ever.

beats.headline: A saddle from the fans
beats.text: Mordecai's constitution potions give me one point, which is a waste, and then three. Then my Platinum fan box opens and our fans have given me a saddle! The Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle, adjusted to fit a cat, matching his feathers. Fifteen percent more spell damage for me, twenty percent more constitution for Mongo. Thank you everybody, I love you all so much! Carl puts it on him, and it clicks into place, and Mongo howls and bounces around the room trying to get it off. Carl says to wait until he is used to it. Oh, all right.

beats.headline: A skull on the dance floor
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut is on the Desperado Club dance floor with the Sledge, plastered on two or three cherries, while Carl talks at the bar. He looks away for a second. When he looks back, both her bodyguards are on their backs, her health is in the deep red, and her Cockroach skill has fired, sparing her the first killing blow. The front of her is covered in blood. A human crawler lies in front of her with his throat slashed. He goes still. A single skull forms after her name.

beats.headline: Her first skull
beats.text: I never wanted to get a skull. The lady cast a spell, and my guy and the other rock guy fell, and I fell too, because Sledgie was stunned, and the other one had a knife. Now he is on the floor. Ji-Hoon, a Knife Sharpener. And there is a skull after my name. Nobody is going to like me now. Carl says they attacked me, and nobody will be mad, and he is positive. I didn't want to kill anybody. Maybe those stupid dogs. But not a person. Not a real person.

beats.headline: But a trifle
beats.text: Katia sees the skull and wants to know what happened. Oh, it was but a trifle. A poor crawler thought he could keep up with me, and I accidentally had to rip his throat out. Honestly, I barely remember the incident. I did have a cherry or two too many. Now if you'll excuse me, I have training to do. By the end of the hour my Dodge is seven, which means I get into that locked door at the club. Then Mongo and I work on riding. We have a psychic bond. Carl has never been a mother, so he wouldn't understand.

beats.headline: Jump ahead on the fast trains
beats.text: The engineer's key will only open engines on the ochre line, and crashing a train to get one stops the trains. So, Carl, doesn't it only stop the trains behind it? We get the key, jump on the Nightmare Express or one of those other super-fast loop trains, go ahead up the line, and catch one of the trains that were already in front. Carl says that's brilliant and scratches my head.

beats.headline: Princess D'nadia, and the Donut Holes
beats.text: Carl, Carl, I hit level twenty-eight and I got a sponsor, and it's Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom! I love her. Carl doesn't even remember who she is, so I make him apologise, because she is probably watching right now. He sat right next to her on Ripper Wonton's show. People watching our feed will see our sponsors' commercials, and I hope she has lots of different ones. My fans should have a name. The Princess Patrol, or something. Carl suggests the Donut Holes. Don't be crude, Carl.

beats.headline: You are making her change
beats.text: We are in the dark tunnel waiting for the train, and Carl says Katia is a big girl who can take care of herself. Then why does he keep telling her what to do? He didn't even ask her if she wanted to get giant. He just shoved the backpack at her. He says look who's talking, me with the boots and the purple mohawk. That's different. Fashion is different from making someone change. He says I'm right, and next time he'll ask her. Good boy, Carl.

beats.headline: The Princess Donut goggles
beats.text: My first benefactor box is the greatest prize in the history of prizes. Princess D'nadia had it made especially for me: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles, a unique item, personally signed. They turn my Magic Missile into a laser, and I can shoot four at the same time, into four train doors at once. Plus they're beautiful. I look like Miss Beatrice. Also I went up two levels to thirty, my charisma hit a hundred, and I picked Love Vampire, which Mordecai told me to get.

beats.headline: Minion Army, read already
beats.text: Remember the tome of Minion Army from the Beguiler Box on the first floor? It costs fifty spell points. With our rest and shower buffs I have fifty-two, so I looked. And of course I read it, Carl. Mordecai isn't here, so we're talking about it now. Five minutes to cast, stuck in place the whole time, and at level one each mob has a two percent chance to change sides. Carl says don't cast it unless he tells me to. Don't be so pessimistic, Carl.

beats.headline: The tower controls
beats.text: I'll go up the chain. Carl is the only one who can drive, and Mongo would be ready to graduate college by the time he got up there. From Widget's tower I can see really far. It smells awful. How many lotion containers does one gremlin need? There are multiple control panels and nothing is labeled. Whoops, that one tipped over a freight car. Then the turntable, one slot over, and it lines up. I opened the gate already, by accident, and more ghouls walked out. I didn't tell Carl straight away, because he might get mad.

beats.headline: Rid of both of them
beats.text: On the undersea show I tell the universe the real reason cocker spaniels keep winning Crufts, because it is the truth that needs to be told, CARL. Afterwards, in the green room, he brings up the coupons. I already know he will, because Imani is a big gossip and messaged me to apologize for telling him. I got rid of them. I buried his under a train track and threw Katia's in the garbage at the Hotdog on a Stick place. And quite frankly, it is a subject I would rather not talk about.

beats.headline: I saw it with my sunglasses
beats.text: In the middle of the horde Hekla shoots Katia with an invisible arrow. I see it through my sunglasses, mixed in with her regular ones, going into Katia's scoop. The first time I think it is a mistake. Then she does it again. I tell Carl, and he tells Katia to lose her mass, and we pull the arrows out of her shoulder, and he tells me to be cool, because this does not have to turn into a fight. Then I tell Hekla exactly what she tried to do, and put a full-strength Magic Missile into her face.

beats.headline: You pretend to be good
beats.text: Hekla corrects me: bolts, not arrows. I will never team up with her. She tells me to breathe. I used to think Hekla was awesome. She is just like all the rest. She told Katia she wanted her, she made her feel special and loved, and all she wanted was to use her and trade her in. Katia did her best. She did not do anything wrong. It is not fair. Now Hekla leans on the wall and lights a cigarette.

beats.headline: Three Heklas in the cab
beats.text: Hekla is dead on the floor and the Daughters are pouring in, so I cast Second Chance on her corpse, and then Clockwork Triplicate on my new minion, and now there are three Heklas. One throws Eva out of the window. The others push everybody back through the door, and the Daughters scream about desecration. Afterwards Katia says she did not mean to kill her. I didn't mean to kill that guy either, I tell her. But he had it coming, and Hekla had it coming even worse.

beats.headline: A pile of hats, in tribute
beats.text: CARL throws thirty of our hats on the ground for stragglers, and I have to tell him there is a fine line between being helpful and being a fool. Millions of gold, Carl. Then Bautista takes off his own hat and sets it in front of me, and suddenly there is a line of people, and every one of them bows and puts a hat down and says thank you, Princess. It is not necessary, I tell them. It was nothing. Our pleasure. I gather every single one into my inventory.

beats.headline: Catching the staff up
beats.text: Mordecai is back, and he has missed a great deal, so I start with what matters. My sunglasses, from Princess D'nadia, which are the only reason we knew Hekla was trying to kill Katia. My charisma is over a hundred. And I took the Love Vampire skill, exactly as he told me. I have cast it a few times, but it has never triggered, because we have been very careful to keep me from getting hit. He tells me to slow down. I tell him to wait until he hears about Katia on the front of a train.

beats.headline: The last Puddle Jump of the floor
beats.text: The dog woman with the flamethrower shot my monster after I said I had the one on the left, and then she said I did not call it, and she is not a he, and I should go to a different position, cat. CARL made me move. Then Katia blasts down a hallway, Carl throws two boom jugs, and I count down from three and Puddle Jump us back to the main room. That was my last one for the floor. We are all burning. I tell the dog woman she is welcome. She grunts.

beats.headline: He called me delightful
beats.text: I insist on being the one to look through the hole, and CARL fusses about my whiskers. The boss is hair and quivering skin, like a man whose pants do not cover his behind, and I get an achievement just for looking at it. Then I lean in and hit it with a double shot, a full-powered Magic Missile stored in my glasses, and the portal takes it. On the other side is Prepotente, who says I am even more delightful in person and wishes to share a brandy with me. He called me delightful!

beats.headline: Not Miss Beatrice
beats.text: Carl scratches me, and I purr, and then he tells me I should not have come for him: we risked ourselves, and the cart. I was not going to abandon him. Who does he think I am, Miss Beatrice? He agrees that I am most definitely not. Then I remember we never sold my hats, and he says they will be collectibles on the next floor. We will be millionaires. And then Loita messages that Odette is waiting, and will not tell me where Zev is.

beats.headline: A reeducation retreat
beats.text: Loita says Zev is taking time off at a reeducation retreat and that Loita is our PR agent now. There are no snacks. I tell Carl we only work with Zev, and he tells me we need to pick our battles. On air there is a video of Carl and that silly pig boy, and I am in it, and nobody will show it to me. After, I ask what reeducation means. Carl says nothing good. I know we are not supposed to like the bad guys, but Zev is my friend. We are going to write a TV show together.

beats.headline: The wheel lands on Air
beats.text: I am team leader, so I spin. Land, Sea, Air or Subterranean: it nearly stops on Sea, then ticks over to Air. Maybe I can pick a class that flies this floor. The second wheel chooses our opponent, and I was hoping for the foxes, but it stops on the Dirigible Gnomes, and we must storm their castle in the sky. The door opens on sand and hot wind. It looks like a giant litterbox. I am very excited. Come on, team. Let's go kill some gnomes.

beats.headline: Glass Cannon, minus the constitution
beats.text: I have to pick a new class the minute we arrive, and the choices are all different, and nobody gives a princess enough time. Mordecai likes Glass Cannon: plus fifteen constitution to replace the ten I lost with Football Hooligan, faster training on all my spells, cheaper spells, and a much stronger Magic Missile. I chose it. I got everything. Except the plus fifteen constitution. Now Mordecai says I am to be kept out of harm's way until I have better armor, and no more riding Mongo into battle. Also the sand is ruining my fur.

beats.headline: Astral Paw, and no swimming
beats.text: My spellbook of the floor is a good one this time, and I read it before Carl can make his speech. Astral Paw. Mordecai says it's a utility spell like Hole, with more force than Astral Hand, and claws at level five. Carl says that at home I could finally knock the vase off the high shelf. That vase was haunted. Then a boss box gives me a Scroll of Water Breathing, and I announce that cats do not swim and it is not going to happen. Mordecai tells me not to say that sort of thing out loud.

beats.headline: We'll be there, Carl
beats.text: Carl asks nicely, and Louis asks whether he's going to blow them up. So I jump onto their table, which scatters their glasses and spills vodka everywhere, and I explain. Carl won't hurt them. But anyone who isn't part of the team will be kicked out of town, and I haven't seen a mob out there lower than level thirty, and these two chuckleheads are level twenty-two. Then I tell them exactly what to say. We'll be there, Carl. Louis says it. Lovely. Chuckleheads is from the AI, not Elle. I've been waiting to use it.

beats.headline: Fourth, and not moving
beats.text: Prepotente is crazy. Carl is crazy too. Lucia is something different; she's insane. And when she threw that boy across the room, nobody stayed for him except Ifechi, which is sad. I call dibs on the dogs. Then the new top ten goes up: Carl second, me fourth, and Katia gone from the list entirely, which is outrageous, because she was a superstar. Katia says thank god. Why didn't I go up? We're separated. This is not acceptable, Carl. And Florin fell down the list, after something that sad. They're punishing him for it.

beats.headline: Hole, applied to a door
beats.text: Carl says he'll have to blow the door. Don't be so dramatic, Carl. I snap off my Hole and cast it again a few inches to the right, so it takes both deadbolts and part of the wall, and the door swings open with a half-moon bite out of it. Glass Cannon makes the spell reach right through. Then Carl tells me to kill the spell, so I do, and the missing piece of door comes back wrong and breaks its own bolts. That was Carl's fault. Then Louis calls me Cat. I am Princess Donut, you buffoon.

beats.headline: The highest bid ever
beats.text: My new sponsor is Veriluxx RealPet Companions, which sounds just awesome, except they sponsor a bunch of other people too, and Princess D'Nadia just sponsored five more. Then Loita says my bidding war lasted until the final possible microsecond and was the highest sponsorship bid ever, beating Carl and Prepotente. That is pretty much what I expected. I ask how Zev is. Twice. She is still in treatment. My sponsor is sending me a product sample, and Carl and Mongo and I are going on a program about it. Do you think there'll be a script? Will I get lines?

beats.headline: Eight more visits
beats.text: Katia and I spent the whole storm at the Desperado Club, and Katia came back in a feather boa, and Mongo has one on his collar that he keeps biting. Eight more visits and I get a free dance. Carl wants to know how much we're spending. Carl, guess what? I got another box from Princess D'Nadia. It's only a bronze this time, but I bet it'll be awesome. The product sample hasn't come yet. Loita says the sponsor wants to make sure we survive the bombing first. Isn't that exciting?

beats.headline: The glasses see heat
beats.text: Princess D'Nadia's box was empty. Then my sunglasses got an update: surface and subsurface temperatures, in precise detail. At the town gate I can tell two of the guards are different from the others. Earlier I stole Skarn's telescope in ten seconds flat; I forgot to leave the thirty gold. Out here it's five degrees hotter in the middle of the bowl than at the edges, which is not acceptable. Then Carl fires a missile right next to me. I'm flammable, Carl. And I don't think I did anything productive in that battle.

beats.headline: You could cook an egg on him
beats.text: Through my glasses Henrik's head glows hotter than anybody's; you could cook an egg on it. Carl needs a boost from my charm, so I tell Henrik we can save the town and we don't care which of them are camels. He shows us the watch. At the Toe, Juice Box's head is just as hot, and the bartender is one too, which is just sneaky. Then Mordecai puts a movie on the screen, and he has a whole library. I have to know how There's Something About Mary ends. Also Louis taught me janky. I'm allowed to have friends, Carl.

beats.headline: The famed healer of Queen Anne
beats.text: The gnome ambassador wants to know which of us is the healer, and it is I, Princess Donut, the famed healer of Queen Anne. I ask for passage onto the Wasteland and mention that my manservant is a world-renowned masseuse, an expert with feet. CARL tells me to stick to the script. Wynne is only a head I raised with Second Chance, and I have never resurrected just a head before. They are a lot more surly. When Leon asks what the potion is, I do not hesitate: Healer's Respite. Stichberries boiled with iron slivers and manticore shavings. It is Mountain Dew.

beats.headline: A hole in the basket
beats.text: Katia tells me to make sure she is secure before I do it, because it is a long drop. I cast Hole on the bottom of the basket, a meter and a half wide now that I have practiced, and all three gnomes fall out with the most astonished faces. Level 34! Then I send two clockwork Mongos off the edge after the next balloon, and it goes past us with a bloody basket and one of Mongo's brothers screeching hello. Level 35. By the time I climb out of my hole in the sand, I have my benefactor box and level 36.

beats.headline: I have merch
beats.text: My benefactor box from Veriluxx RealPet Companions opens, and it is me. A robot me, three-quarters size, with fur like rat hair, and it says it likes lasagna and hates Mondays. Katia says they mixed me up with Garfield. They made a doll out of me. It is merch. I have merch. It is the greatest thing since I won Grand Champion Best in Show in Cleveland. Then it asks Mongo whether he is a cocker spaniel, Mongo bites its head off, it catches fire, and a static shock hits me on the nose. This is most certainly going into my review.

beats.headline: Don't be mad at me
beats.text: Carl forms his fist to kill Chris himself, and everyone else steps back. Don't be mad at me, I tell him, and I open a Hole under Chris, and he drops through into the dark room underneath with a splash. Carl only falls about a foot, onto the quadrant's forcefield, and I tell him to step out before his feet get chopped off. He says that was a mistake. It was not. Carl is not a killer. Not a person killer. I am not going to let him kill one of his friends, because I cannot have him being all mopey.

beats.headline: My heal spell stopped working
beats.text: The goose turns off magic, and the two clockwork Mongos explode early and hurt my baby. My heal spell will not work. My Heal Critter scroll fizzles. My pet carrier does not work. Mongo is bleeding and his health keeps going down, and CARL shouts at me to use a bandage, so I do, and it works. I rip a hole in the bedroom floor so we can drop back into the kitchen. And who flips the garbage disposal switch while Carl holds the goose's head in the sink? Me.

beats.headline: What they did to Zev
beats.text: The fish lady will not let me bring Mongo to meet his own doll, and then she tells us why she is so angry. We are dry. We are a rot. And to bring Zev back into the fold, they did unspeakable things to her mother and her aunts, and only then did Zev take the badge. I ask Carl whether she is a complete loon. On set, a lady in a cow-print cape says I am one of her two favorites; the other is Lucia Mar. I read my line: This sure is a hoot. Then the lights go red, and I cannot cast a thing.

beats.headline: He had Tish all along
beats.text: The letter from the council is appalling. Ghazi had Tish the whole time, and he left her for Lika, who is a character in a play. When he wakes up I jump on his chest and tell him exactly that. Then he admits the sand ooze is his wife, because he married it, and that the Lika in the fountain was a companion device. Everybody has worked out what kind. I am the first one to say it out loud, because somebody has to.

beats.headline: I bite his foot and pull
beats.text: The floor breaks right after I cast my Hole spell, and I fall through with it, and there is sand all around me. Carl is buried upside down, so I bite down on his foot and drag him out. Then we are in a tiny space under three floors of sand, and I did not get to say goodbye to Mongo, and he is just going to sit in his pet carrier forever. And all Carl will ask me is how many water-breathing scrolls I have. Eight.

beats.headline: Worse than the danger dingo
beats.text: I wake up underwater. Completely underwater. I cannot swim; my legs only tread. I stop screaming only because Carl says Mongo needs me. Then I see a shark down there, and more coming, which is a betrayal worse than when he gave my pet biscuits to that danger dingo. Then he says "Hekla", so I cast Second Chance on a dead beluga and Clockwork Triplicate on top, and send them at the shark, and they explode. In the kayak a small fish comes out of me. The box gives me a Belt of Buoyancy. I am never going back there.

beats.headline: In charge of the death charges
beats.text: Carl says I take two or three showers a day, so the ocean is no different. It is entirely different, and it is not happening again, and there is not a thing in this world he can say to change my mind. Then he admits he is teasing. I will only have to float over the water in the house and be in charge of the depth charges. I do like the death charges. And since Zev has her job back, I can check my social media board again.

beats.headline: Shuruga36
beats.text: A viewer called Shuruga36 says I have no redeeming qualities whatsoever, that I ruined the viewing experience and almost made him stop watching, and that Donut and her stupid dino-chicken irritate him to no end. Mongo is a child. I can take criticism, but picking on a child is uncalled for. Then I hit the detonator for the chum bombs and go up a level, to 38. Before they drop, I tell Carl and Katia to be safe, because it is horrible down there.

beats.headline: Up a level for doing nothing
beats.text: Carl wants to know if we are almost back. We are not. The wind starts early and blows wrong, Firas says, and we keep getting higher and higher, so we have to go back to Hump Town, and Louis says ten minutes. Then I go up a level, and I did not even do anything. I should stay back more often. This is great. When Carl finally falls into the personal space he is sopping wet. He smells terrible, and he has seaweed in his hair.

beats.headline: Juice Box is remembering
beats.text: Carl, remember Fire Brandy and that dwarf, when they started to remember? It is happening to Juice Box. When we told her that her brother had died she was sad at first, and then she got really happy. She has been dreaming that she was a school teacher, and some people came in and had to kill all her students because the children were spreading a disease, and she touched one of them, a dragon-headed man. Louis told her she might be remembering her last time in the dungeon. She got a funny look on her face.

beats.headline: The quest chat, and the flying house
beats.text: CARL wants me to keep the revolting two-headed dog alive, because I am the only one with the spell. Then there is a quest chat, with everybody in the bubble on it, and Maggie My is on it, so I tell her exactly what she is. Worse than the lady who fed Peanut's Splendid Flavor no meat. Worse than all of them combined. Chris keeps typing my name. Then the spell says I am too far away from the dog, so I go up in the flying house with Louis and Firas, in a storm. Heal Critter works. I cannot believe it. The stupid dog does not even appreciate it.

beats.headline: Meat Hooks, with no off button
beats.text: CARL is flying the drop bear, and I am in the seat behind him with my Torch stuck to the wing so we can see. I heal the mountain of a puppy twice on a pass behind its heads. Then he circles round and I read the Meat Hooks scroll, which smells like the worst thing that has ever happened. It works. The puppy comes after the smoke, straight out of the bubble. Then it is catching up, and CARL says to turn the spell off, and there is no button. There is always a button. The smoke will not stop.

beats.headline: Thumbs, Carl
beats.text: CARL locks the plane onto its little autopilot, jumps out on the wing and yells at me to grab the stick. Grab the stick. I do not have thumbs. I grab it anyway, with everything, and we roll and corkscrew, and something falls off the back. Then he is glowing, and I am on his back with my claws in, and we jump. When I wake up I am singed and he is holding a man's arm. I have decided something. He is crazy. Not a little weird crazy. Not cereal-without-milk crazy. Straitjacket crazy.

beats.headline: Maggie's hats
beats.text: GIRL FIGHT. Then CARL is unconscious with a hole in his neck, so I heal him with a scroll, and Chris too. I looted Maggie the first time Mongo threw her up. She had a lot of stuff. A lot of hats. CARL says give it all to Chris. What does Chris need with a bunch of hats? I collect hats. Then Juice Box says she is marrying Louis. The whole world has gone insane. And everyone is going to be hunting us, and I do not like people hunting us, CARL.

beats.headline: Legendary Diva
beats.text: I have the world's greatest class for this floor, and I will tell CARL only if he promises not to get mad. Katia says he is going to be mad. I am a bard. A Legendary Diva. I sing songs and they cast spells, and I got a bunch of them. They said I could permanently pick any class I already had, and Mordecai told me not to, so I did not. The tree man at the pub says I can have a gig for the lunch shift. Katia says after the lunch shift. Don't ruin it, Katia.

beats.headline: Small, adorable, and a rescuer
beats.text: Carl called for help at the village entrance and I came on Mongo. Low-powered magic missiles make the invisible weasels show themselves; one of them caught fire from the gunpowder on its fur. When one died I raised it and cast Clockwork Triplicate on it and told it to get them. Then a guard spewed a poison cloud and we had to run. And now Carl is on the floor laughing at Mordecai. You shouldn't make fun of someone just because they're small and adorable. I'm small and adorable, and I just saved your life.

beats.headline: A singer who must be in key
beats.text: My bard spells don't use mana. I only have to sing them, in key, and the spell is only as strong as the singing. Standing Ovation, Entourage and Encore I can manage if I sing the words in a steady monotone, so they are weak. The two attack songs I cannot manage at all. Katia and Chris left on the caravan, and Katia kissed me on the head. What if something happens to her and we can't protect her? Mongo would never forgive me. Then Mordecai and I went shopping for a Golden Throat enchantment, and there was none.

beats.headline: A move, not a plan
beats.text: Predator, Carl says, two seconds before we land in the hunters' city. That is not a plan, Carl. That is a move. We go invisible, I call out what my sunglasses see, I puddle jump us past a park full of traps, and then a barrel goes off outside the saferoom and blows us across the bar. I think I want to go to Katia's team now. Instead we run, and I try to sing Entourage on his shoulder, which is like karaoke on a rollercoaster, and an invisible hunter on a roof fills him with crossbow bolts.

beats.headline: Hunter Killer, once
beats.text: There is a red dagger spinning after my name now: Hunter Killer times one. It was nothing, a magic missile while we were running away, and I think Carl's explosion really killed him, but they gave me the credit. Carl was in a coma for half an hour. Miriam, Prepotente and Bianca saved him, so he must say thank you, and he must be nice to Prepotente, who does not like him. From now on I am not participating in a Carl plan unless I know what I am getting myself into. Mongo is quite upset with him.

beats.headline: A pet beauty contest
beats.text: The party at the end of this floor has a pet beauty contest, and Mongo is going to follow in Mommy's pawsteps. We will need an extra hour of training a day, a seamstress, a walk coach, the upgraded pet shower to get the blood out, and the standards manual immediately. Carl should message his attorney. And he may not say we are not doing this. I have very little, and this is something we are going to do. Very well, Carl. But we are going to need more hands, and the guild immediately.

beats.headline: A clockwork Bomo
beats.text: Carl wants to send Bomo out as a suicide bomber. Bomo is our friend. We don't blow up our friends, Carl. It isn't a suicide bombing if he comes back next floor, he says, and Bomo seemed excited. It won't work. They'll be waiting for him. So what if I made a clockwork Bomo? He'd have to be switched to a minion of me and not the party, like Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and then I can make copies. Really, Carl. Pay attention to how the party system works. I just have to be in the saferoom.

beats.headline: I have my own town
beats.text: The town rules say no dinosaurs of any kind, no exceptions. They specifically called out Mongo. I demand the person in charge, and the mushroom actually goes and gets him. The mayor thinks I am a monkey. Carl agrees to pay him a hundred and fifty gold to have us both executed, the mayor steps closer to take it, and I cast Astral Paw. He rolls down the slope and finds every rock on it. Something from the river takes the body. I got the credit. My own town! I'm going to make dancing mandatory.

beats.headline: Mayor Donut, briefly
beats.text: The system made me Mayor Donut, and I changed it back to Princess immediately. To order the guards about I must wear a new collar charm, and the gem is turquoise. Turquoise! Do I look like a woman in a bingo hall? I have removed all of those idiotic rules except the bugbear one, until Carl said it was a trap. I have named the officers and sergeants: Dinallo, Miss Nance, Doctor El. I absolutely will not reintroduce a racist policy to make a bunch of overgrown teddy bears comfortable. The town is named after a dinosaur.

beats.headline: Everybody always leaves me
beats.text: I'm supposed to pretend like I don't know. And I was doing good. Then Mongo ran off, and it was Miss Beatrice's car accident on the way back from the cat show all over again, me slamming into the side of the carrier. Everybody always leaves me. Am I really that awful? Katia left us. Carl keeps doing more dangerous things. Mongo is going to leave for some hussy. And what about the ninth floor? Carl holds my face and says he will not leave me behind, on the ninth or any other floor. No matter what.

beats.headline: Out of tune, apparently
beats.text: The murder weasels attack from three sides, and I start singing Standing Ovation, which would have given everyone a dexterity boost. It fails. Afterward Holger, whose face is swollen shut from fighting his own friend, informs me that I cannot sing in tune. He says there is no shame in it. The easy spells simply fail, but try something big off-key and it becomes dangerous, so I need lessons. It is very hard to sing properly with all that grunting and stabbing going on. Besides, Carl and Mongo think I am an excellent singer.

beats.headline: It is my decision
beats.text: Odette says Miss Beatrice is alive and wants her on the show, and Carl tells Odette where to go and that we are not going out there. I say we are. It is my decision. Carl wants to do it alone, to protect me, and I remind him what I told him before: we need to trust each other. It is going to happen one way or another, so at least now we have a moment to prepare. I thank Odette for saving her from becoming a dungeon boss, and for the warning. Then I find the treats in the pink bag under the counter.

beats.headline: Not my person anymore
beats.text: On air I lick my paw. I tell her to have a good life, to buy only the wet food, and not to pretend to love a cat she means to sell. Then Odette says we are off the air, and I tell Miss Beatrice what she is. She danced with me and sang to me and was my whole world, and she was going to give me away. What she did to Carl was not okay either. I still love her, and I hate myself for it. She does not get to explain. You're not my person anymore. Carl is. He's always been.

beats.headline: What she smuggled
beats.text: In the green room Lexis tells us about the elf queen and the party, and says the Valtay will want to wipe out the top of the leaderboard and start fresh. That is most distressing. I certainly would never have smuggled all those Valtay secret agent guys to Zev and the Borant Emancipation Front if I had known this was going to happen. Lexis stares at me with her mouth open. Carl says 'What?' and then we are transferred. Back in the saferoom he tells me not to say a word. Relax, Carl. Everything will be okay.

beats.headline: The Raggle Rouser
beats.text: Carl holds out a bracelet from the dead elf. Black, glass, a plain bangle, and then I read the description. Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser: ten constitution, five dexterity, fifteen percent fire resistance, and a level-10 Fireball once every twenty minutes. Give it to me now, Carl. It appears on my front right leg, much smaller, and I move it to my front left. He tells me not to use a fireball in a tight space, because it is more dangerous than magic missile. I know how fire works, Carl.

beats.headline: Goddess of unrequited love
beats.text: Carl says we have never learned what Samantha is supposed to be the goddess of. I asked her, Carl. She says unrequited love. I must say, I get the impression it is more like the goddess of crazy ex-girlfriends. Everything she does is because she wants to get back with some king. She also thinks her sand ooze child, the one married to the mage on the last floor, is alive and on the ninth floor. She wants to pick the child up and then get down to wherever the king is. The first part of her plan is a body.

beats.headline: Fireball is awesome
beats.text: Carl's shield throws the disgusting thing straight up, which is not to the side, Carl. He shouts at me to shoot. Fireball! The level-10 ball rises slowly, almost reluctantly, and blasts into its pink stomach, and the whole creature catches alight and lands splat on the shield, sliding off face down against the trees, firing lightning everywhere. Wow. Fireball is awesome. Then Mongo dives for the wound with me still on his back, and I backflip onto Carl's shoulder, firing one last magic missile.

beats.headline: Never alone with her
beats.text: Signet wants to jump Carl's bones, and if I know anything, it is how story arcs work. Before the final battle there will be a meadow and a ring of flowers in her hair and candles and butterflies, and afterward they will try to kill him. Sex with a guest star always spells doom. Well, I am not going to let it happen. He is never to be alone with her again. Carl says he is not going to boink Signet. No, he is not. Not if I have anything to say about it.

beats.headline: Lucia's traps in the doorways
beats.text: Lucia is in the saferoom, screeching and punching herself in the face, waiting for me to come out. She has found a way to cheat the safety measures: traps that kick people out of the room. I went out when I thought she was gone, hit one, and landed in the middle of town, and then I hit another, and she came out of the woods and chased me inside just as the hunters arrived. So now I am in the guildhall, trying to give CARL important backstory.

beats.headline: A vocal coach of her own
beats.text: My platinum box gave me a vocal coach. A whole little room, with a microphone behind glass and a holographic lady called Lover Illiana who says I have a voice like a cygnus cloud gull. My singing is already level four. Mordecai says it is a great prize, even if we still need to discuss the name of the box. Then Carl finally works out what my useless Scutelliphily potion was for. Patches. Embroidery. Carl, I think you're right!

beats.headline: Cici, and the Hole spell
beats.text: The recap shows the whole thing, and I am magnificent in it. Lucia swaps places with me so I land between her two rottweilers, and I backflip off the big one. She snares me in the treehouse pub. So I sing, and Entourage gives five Donuts, one laid over myself, and I drink invisibility and cast Hole under my own feet. Cici sticks her head down the hole. I close it. Her head drops into the mud. The only bridge she'll cross today is made of rainbows.

beats.headline: Not a drop of Mongo
beats.text: The Apothecary sent me a gold box, and in it a silver bracelet with little purple garlic gems that protects against vampirism. It is divine, even if the description reads like the AI is having a stroke. Then Carl and Mordecai read a recipe and look at Mongo. A liter of his blood. Per potion. Absolutely not. I am Mongo's mommy, and he trusts me implicitly. Mongo, come here this instant where Mommy can protect you. Mordecai says he'll make him sleep. I'll know, Mordecai.

beats.headline: It is my town now
beats.text: The dryad mayor offered me 5,000 gold to tie Carl up and bring him out. I'd have fireballed him on the spot, but the guards were all outside. So I filled a liter of Mongo in the rain, cutting and healing him three times, with wet monkeys holding the flask, because I don't have thumbs. Then at the western gate Carl said be careful, just the mayor, magic missile, not a... and I cast Fireball. It squeezed between two guards and hit him. Half the town burned. In the rain! It's my town now.

beats.headline: She reads the spellbook anyway
beats.text: Miriam drops a spellbook at her feet and says I must read it to wake Prepotente up. Carl says wait. I do not wait: I cast Second Chance on a raccoon and have it fetch the spellbook, and I read it. Get Out of Jail, forty points, which is a lot. Then Carl tells me she wants us to kill her, and that if she dies everyone infected is cured and Prepotente can heal. I do not want to kill either of them. This is just like with Chris.

beats.headline: Rules for Kiwi
beats.text: I told Carl I am quite practised at taming dinosaurs, and I am. I walk up to Kiwi alone, tail straight, and she glows, and she is my minion. Rule number one is not to molest Mongo again. Rule number two is not to eat Carl. Then I let Mongo out and it all goes wrong at once, and so much for rule number one. And a terrible thought: did the Plenty want Miriam to die? Carl says yes.

beats.headline: She catches the lightning
beats.text: The queen's familiar talks to us from a curtained box on a rhinoceros, in a creepy voice, and says I am to dance with him at the Masquerade. Then the curtain moves and lightning comes straight at Mongo, and I jump in front of it. I am knocked out for a minute. Carl says I saved Mongo's life. I heal them both, and then I tell Carl what I saw through the curtain. It was Ferdinand.

beats.headline: A mother now, over it
beats.text: We are not going down the stairs early, Carl. It is not even a discussion. Ferdinand may have been my first love, but I am a mother now, and I have more important responsibilities. Mongo needs me, and if I am going to pursue a singing career I cannot be all emotional because my ex-boyfriend is suddenly trying to get back into the picture. It surprised me, I admit. If Taylor Swift or Adele can profit off heartache, so can I. It will make a good song.

beats.headline: You're acting weird
beats.text: Carl has his foot on a hunter's chest and he is talking to him. He is doing it again. He is the one who says it is too dangerous to keep them alive, and I tell him so: kill him now. He does not. He pulls a nipple ring out with his toe and pours a potion on the man's face and listens to him for ages. Carl, are you okay? You are acting weird.

beats.headline: Bribed with his sponsor prize
beats.text: It is a nipple ring and it dangles, and one does not pierce the nipples of cats. Then Carl offers me his sponsor prize, a potion of plus three to any spell, and Carl never gives up his prizes. I am almost at twelve in Magic Missile. Mordecai looks at him strangely. Fine, but he goes first. And do not tell Katia. I do not want her thinking I am a whore. He does his own, and I do not think I can respect him anymore. Top right, Carl.

beats.headline: Tina as a backup dancer
beats.text: They accepted my applications! Both of them! The talent show rejected Carl's version because a crawler has to be the star, so I will be the star. I am going to sing, and Kiwi and Tina and the rest of the crew will be my backup dancers. Carl says he does not think that will work. Do not be such a Debbie Downer, Carl. Mongo, we're in! Mommy is going to sing, and you are going to win the beauty contest.

beats.headline: My Katia?
beats.text: Carl says so, you and Katia, to Bautista, and Bautista says it just sort of happened. My Katia? Does she know this? Carl says it has been obvious for a while. Katia is outside. This is just as surprising as Louis and Juice Box. Carl, are you going to allow this to continue? Bautista thought Carl had a thing for her, which is silly. Carl is psychologically damaged thanks to Miss Beatrice, and I had no idea Katia was into furries.

beats.headline: The ledger, privately
beats.text: Clarabelle will not let us down to the Hunting Grounds level, and she is insulted when I mention a hundred gold. She has misunderstood. My interface keeps track of every gold piece I have ever spent. Five hundred gold, paid to Clarabelle for private secure escorts, the day I met Sledgie. A refund from Astrid of only four hundred. Carl has a kind heart, and he thought we should take the matter up with her privately. I look at the door. This is us, taking the matter up privately.

beats.headline: He is trying to warn us
beats.text: Carl was out for forty-five minutes, and they let me order from the kitchen. Capers are really gross. Orren talks and talks about liaisons and the spirit of the game, and Carl asks what in the flying fuck he is talking about. It is obvious. He is trying to warn us about something, but he is struggling because he does not like us and he is scared of breaking the rules. They both stare at me. Orren says he likes us quite a bit.

beats.headline: He did not count to three
beats.text: The costumes are ready. Mordecai helped with the bubbles for Kiwi's, but my clam does not like her outfit and miss seaweed's falls off every time they practise the jump. They let me dress them because they trust me. Once trust is broken it can never be replaced, Carl. If someone says they will count to three, one expects them to count to three. You're lucky the saferoom froze me. I almost bit your hand off. He says I have a saferoom strike now.

beats.headline: Not the Stupid Dictator Carl
beats.text: I got five kills. Five! Good boy, Mongo! Good girl, Kiwi! Then Carl sees his mark and tells me to take both potions right now, and my cooldown has a minute and forty-five seconds left, and the god runs off anyway. Carl says when he tells me to do something I have to do it immediately. The last I looked, this was the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Not the Stupid Team of Stupid Dictator Carl and his Abused Slave Cat, Princess Donut.

beats.headline: The tiara helps
beats.text: Tina keeps wandering off from the caravan, so I am outside keeping her in line. No, Tina! If you eat the elf he will not let you into the castle! We just gave you a bath! Kiwi, you must keep your child under better control. Carl tells me to put on my new tiara. I already did, and it helps a lot with the dinosaurs, but the guards are agitated. New ones in black jackets. They go into the last cart.

beats.headline: The dinosaurs get the other room
beats.text: The castle elves say my professional show animals must go in cages. Outrageous. The stablemancer, Kibben, says the belly acher would swallow one of my mongoliensis whole, which is a reason to disqualify that walking meatball, not to cage my Mongo. I ask whether my dinosaurs can go to the other attendant ballroom, and Carl tells him the best way to shut me up is to let me have my way. Rude. It works. I insist on watching the transfer.

beats.headline: A stage version of a cocker spaniel
beats.text: The theater is gorgeous at first glance and built by someone who knows nothing about such things. There is no thrust. There are no wings at all. The grid is maybe five feet above the arch, they ignored my request for catwalk access, and the AV elf could not work the boombox. Carl keeps asking about the catwalk. It is catwalk, singular, and it is forward enough; Edgar's map was accurate. It is a stage version of a cocker spaniel. And this is only for Mongo's presentation.

beats.headline: That was low key
beats.text: Louis messed up some of the lines, and Mongo was supposed to leap completely offstage before the moonwalk reveal, but it went almost perfectly. The blob judge was shaking, and I am really sure that is a good thing. Carl says he distinctly remembers saying low-key. That was low key, Carl. They told me I couldn't do the magic missile entrance we planned. This was nothing compared to the Ke$ha act Miss Beatrice and I performed in Cleveland. Wait until they see our real dance number.

beats.headline: She charms Ferdinand
beats.text: My ex-boyfriend lands on Carl in a royal turban with a four-foot feather, and I tell Carl I don't think I can do this; it only worked a little on the elves. Eye on the prize, he says. Remember how he tried to kill Mongo. So I tell everyone to stop making fun of his hat. I like it. It looks quite smart. And it takes. He goes casual, calls me babe, air-humps Carl's head, stays for my performance. Then he offers to come over to our ballroom, and he is gone.

beats.headline: All Eyes on Me
beats.text: I take the charm potion, and it works: Sir Ferdinand, minion of Princess Donut, has joined the party, and he tells the Empress that is his bird up there. Then the spotlight. My name is Princess Donut, and I am singing the song my mother used to sing to me. It is called 'All Eyes on Me.' I do not take out the sheet music. I do not need it. Britney plays. Everyone in the room is charmed, even the hunters, even the queen. And then the spotlight finds Tina.

beats.headline: Sic 'em
beats.text: Sic 'em, I say, and my velociraptors leap off the stage into the hunters. When the queen is busy with Ferdinand and Carl, I call Kiwi to me and tell her to lower her head, and I squeeze the bubble on her neck until the potion ball inside bursts. Kiwi stands up a bear, naked except for her paper bubbles. All my other raptors go red at once. Tina comes back onto the stage, sees her mother, and roars until the roar is words. Mommy?

beats.headline: Laundry Day at fifteen
beats.text: I got top billing, again. Then my Laundry Day. Carl made me train it every day for weeks, to nine, my Pawna's Cries potion made it twelve, and his Pawna's Tears took it to the very end of fifteen. Carl pushes the bugs back with Katia's hat, and Mongo and I jump in, and I cast it at the god in the corner. Soapy bubbles everywhere. Diwata goes back to the Halls of Ascendency, and a wet mantis woman is left standing there, and her own children fall on her.

beats.headline: Why it doesn't hurt
beats.text: We won. Firas is dead, and Gwen, and Horton, and the Popovs. Britney's face stayed gross when we healed it. I cannot stop talking. Then I ask Carl the thing. Why doesn't it hurt as much as it should? They were my friends, and I think I should be crying, and I'm not. Even Florin cried. I think something inside of me has broken. Carl says I'm wearing a mask and it is protecting me. You were right, I tell him. That was way more like Rambo than Footloose. And then I cry.

beats.headline: Viper Queen, and number one
beats.text: Carl, we're in a fish tank! And I'm ranked number one. Number one! I need to pick a new class, and the chat is down so Mordecai can't help, so I pick one. Viper Queen. Doesn't that sound delicious? I can shoot poison blobs. My health is lower, which Prepotente says is of no consequence. Then Prepotente leaves the party, and I am party leader.

beats.headline: Master Telephone Psychic
beats.text: I chose Cuba rather than the Bahamas, and that was strategy: they gave Carl a book about the Bahamas, which was quite obviously a trap. Then ten minutes to pick a class, which is an improvement. Mordecai offers me an Agony Urchin, which changes the way I look, so absolutely not, or Master Telephone Psychic. I pick Psychic. My map now sees the whole building, my intelligence goes up five points, and I get Brain Freeze, Bad Attitude and Why Are You Hitting Yourself?, which makes people stab themselves in the face. I keep the Viper Queen's poison spit, too.

beats.headline: The first newsletter
beats.text: The first newsletter of my one official fan club goes out, and I absolutely do not approve of the name the Donut Holes. I recap the last few floors as best I can: Signet's revenge, Mongo and Kiwi killing Vrah, the whole castle sent down with our army in it. Then the crime of the century. Tserendolgor got her hands on the pet show ballot box and handed Mongo's crown to her disgusting meatball pet. I want the footage pored over until someone finds the smoking gun. Remember to pay your dues. The Team Mongo Mommies tier is twenty credits a week extra.

beats.headline: A nipple ring and a screaming book
beats.text: No spellbook of the floor for the seventh, which is an outrage, only one for Mute. Then my boxes. A cosmic buff potion that gives me dexterity instead of charisma. A skill potion that takes Love Vampire from three to six and lets it cast on its own. A nipple ring from a superior fire demon's hand maiden, which has the most sexist description I have ever read, and a berserking spell I will not name that Mordecai says I may only cast by myself. And a chained, quivering tome that screams as I learn it: Legionnaires of the Damned. I have always been badass.

beats.headline: Dibs on the beret
beats.text: Our first mob is a wolf thing with a gigantic bearded head in a glowing red beret, and it screams insults at us in Spanish. A magic missile, a fireball, and then my new Mute spell so it cannot cast. Then I remember Why Are You Hitting Yourself? It works! The monster bites savagely at its own leg until it dies, and I call dibs on the hat. Its inventory holds a combo card, and Carl is told that only the squad leader may hold cards. The beret suits me. I am thinking of embracing the revolutionary look.

beats.headline: A Havana brown, of all things
beats.text: She is a Havana brown. A cat girl, and a Havana brown, and a nun, which is simply too much at once. She says she did not choose the breed, and maybe it is because she is Cuban. Lies! The Havana brown originated in England and has no association with Cuba at all. Then it comes out that they are frightened of me, over something I said ages ago, in confidence, to a dancer at the Desperado Club, about what I would do if I ever met a cat girl. I can't be held accountable for everything I've ever said to a stripper. I suppose I must get over it.

beats.headline: She doesn't use a litterbox
beats.text: Mongo eats a duende whose name is Mordecai, which I wanted to put in our squad. Then the saferoom, a coffee shop, and I invite Sister Ines's group to join our guild. We have a very nice shower, and the beds, and a bopca in the common area, and the upgraded litterbox. She says she does not use a litterbox. I like Paz.
